finding.claim: Default allow_relative_path_traversal=true lets in-root '..' segments resolve silently, so an application that authorizes on the raw path string (e.g. prefix 'users/alice/') can be bypassed to reach 'users/bob/' within the same storage root.
finding.source: Application-supplied path string containing '..' (e.g. 'users/alice/../bob/profile.json'), a precondition rather than a library defect.
finding.sink: Filesystem::write/read/delete and other operations at src/Filesystem.php:53-60 and :84-87 act on the normalized path after the application's raw-string check.

trace.note: Reads allow_relative_path_traversal option, defaulting to true
Only throws when allowRelativePaths is false or stack is empty

finding.guards_checked: Root escape blocked: '..' with empty stack throws PathTraversalDetected (line 40). Backslashes converted to '/' (line 24). Leading slashes dropped. Control characters and invalid UTF-8 rejected (lines 25-29). Not verified: application-side authorization logic, which is outside this code.

finding.claim: Public URLs are built by concatenating the normalized path onto the prefix without percent-encoding, so '%2e%2e' segments, '?' and '#' survive normalization and can make the generated URL resolve to a different object than the one the application intended.
finding.source: Filename or key chosen by an uploader, e.g. '%2e%2e/private/x.pdf', 'a?b' or 'a#b'.
finding.sink: Generated public URL returned by Filesystem::publicUrl and embedded or shared by the application.

trace.note: normalizePath applied; '%2e%2e', '?' and '#' are not structural in WhitespacePathNormalizer so they pass through
prefixPath concatenates the raw path with no percent-encoding

finding.guards_checked: Literal '..' and leading slashes removed by normalizer, so host cannot be switched and literal '..' cannot climb above the prefix. No percent-encoding applied. Impact is limited: the same object is reachable directly from the origin, so the origin's ACL is the real access boundary. Confidence low to medium.
finding.repro: Upload with key 'uploads/%2e%2e/private/x.pdf', then call publicUrl('uploads/%2e%2e/private/x.pdf'). A WHATWG-compliant client normalizes the URL to /private/x.pdf at the origin.

finding.claim: inverseForFile and inverseForDirectory report PUBLIC for any mode that is neither the configured public nor private value, so visibility inspection fails open.
finding.source: Precondition: a file or directory with a non-canonical mode (e.g. 0640 from an external process or permissive umask). The library cannot set modes from attacker input.
finding.sink: Filesystem::visibility at src/Filesystem.php:187-190, which an application may use in an authorization decision.

trace.note: inverseForFile compares only against configured public and private modes
Unknown mode falls through to return Visibility::PUBLIC

finding.guards_checked: PortableVisibilityGuard rejects invalid visibility input on the write side (src/PortableVisibilityGuard.php:9-17). The read-side inference is not guarded. Confidence low; the attacker cannot directly control file modes through this library.
